title: Reception, Admission, Referral and Discharge Procedures
path: Reception, Admission, Referral and Discharge Procedures

headings.title: Reception and Ward Orientation Procedures
headings.content:
When a patient arrives at a healthcare ward, the first impression shapes their entire hospital stay. Nurses must greet the patient warmly, verify their identity using standard hospital protocols, and settle them comfortably into their assigned bed. Ward orientation reduces anxiety by familiarizing the patient and their relatives with the physical environment and hospital routines.

- **Physical Environment**: Show the location of the nursing station, bathroom, emergency call bell, and fire exits.
- **Ward Routines**: Explain times for vital signs measurement, doctor's ward rounds, medication administration, and mealtimes.
- **Personal Belongings**: Guide the patient on securing valuables or cataloging them for safekeeping according to hospital policy.

headings.title: Types and Procedures of Hospital Admission
headings.content:
Hospital admission is the official acceptance of a patient into a bed for diagnosis, treatment, and nursing care. Admissions generally fall into distinct categories based on urgency.

- **Emergency Admission**: Unplanned entry due to acute illness or severe trauma, requiring immediate life-saving interventions.
- **Routine Admission**: Planned entry scheduled in advance for elective surgeries, specialized investigations, or chronic disease management.
- **Transfer Admission**: Movement of a patient into the ward from another hospital department or facility for specialized care.

headings.title: Documentation and Record Keeping During Admission
headings.content:
Accurate documentation during admission forms the legal and clinical bedrock of patient care. The nurse must open a comprehensive case file containing biographical data, consent forms, admission notes, and baseline vital signs. Every entry must be legible, timely, and signed by the attending nurse. 

A common mistake is delaying documentation until the end of a busy shift, which leads to forgotten clinical details. Nurses must record observations promptly to ensure patient safety and maintain clear legal protection for clinical actions taken.

headings.title: Patient Referral Principles and Procedures
headings.content:
Referral involves sending a patient from one level of healthcare to another when the current facility lacks the resources, equipment, or specialized personnel to manage the condition. A valid referral requires effective communication between the referring clinician and the receiving institution. 

The nurse prepares the patient physically and psychologically, ensures all clinical notes, investigation results, and referral letters are complete, and organizes safe transport accompanied by appropriate medical personnel if the patient is unstable.

headings.title: Discharge Planning and Preparation
headings.content:
Discharge planning begins on the day of admission, not the day the patient leaves. It is a coordinated, multidisciplinary process that ensures a smooth transition from the hospital back to the home or another care facility. 

The nurse assesses the patient's post-discharge needs, coordinates with physiotherapists, social workers, and pharmacists, and provides comprehensive health education covering medication adherence, diet, wound care, and follow-up clinic dates.

headings.title: Types of Discharge and Nursing Responsibilities
headings.content:
Patients leave the hospital under various circumstances, each carrying distinct nursing protocols and legal implications.

- **Routine Discharge**: Planned release authorized by the medical team when treatment goals are achieved.
- **Discharge Against Medical Advice (AMA)**: Departure initiated by the patient or family against the doctor's recommendation. The nurse must document the event clearly and have the patient or proxy sign an AMA form.
- **Abscondment**: Unauthorized departure without informing hospital staff. The nurse must notify hospital security and management immediately.
- **Transfer**: Movement to another facility for continued care.
